verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe GoogleSQL as an ANSI-compliant SQL dialect with native query statements, pipe syntax, and procedural extensions. A hands-on review reports native QUALIFY, which points to window-function support, and says pipe syntax makes iterating on arrays and parsing JSON much better. Everything is part of the core engine, with no bolt-on extensions. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of window functions and CTEs, any evidence of rich date/time types, and first-party docs on JSON and array types (these come only from one community review).

support.subject: As an analyst, I get a full analytical SQL surface — window functions, CTEs, semi-structured JSON, arrays, and rich date/time types — without bolt-on extensions

citations.quote: GoogleSQL is an ANSI-compliant Structured Query Language (SQL) that includes the following types of supported statements
Query statements can include pipe syntax.
Procedural language statements are procedural extensions to GoogleSQL that let you execute multiple SQL statements in one request.
It unifies WHERE/HAVING/QUALIFY and makes iterating on arrays and parsing JSON much better.
